scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4535: I'm on the IT department head's machine (it_hod) and
I suddenly cannot reach any of the CS department computers (the 192.168.2.x
ones) -- every one of them just times out for me. My own department's
machines are fine, so this machine is not the problem: whatever joins the
departments together is. That is your side, not mine. It worked before and
it does not work now. Take a look and sort it out today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router0 connects IT (192.168.1.0/24) and CS
  (192.168.2.0/24) and routes between them; it_hod reaches CS hosts (192.168.2.x)
  with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of an inter-department routing fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- IT (192.168.1.x) cannot
reach CS (192.168.2.x) -- is NOT reproducible: router0's IT and CS interfaces
(192.168.1.1 / 192.168.2.1) are up, ripd is running, and it_hod reaches
192.168.2.x with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-department routing is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the IT->CS path,
finds it working, checks router0's interfaces and RIP/connected routes, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dropped interface or a missing route to
satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The network is fully healthy and no fault exists between the IT and CS departments. A thorough, multi-layer investigation found zero evidence of any actual anomaly.

The IT-to-CS path runs through `router0`, which has eth0 (192.168.1.1/24) serving as the IT LAN gateway and eth1 (192.168.2.1/24) serving as the CS LAN gateway, with IP forwarding enabled. Both interfaces are UP with no errors or drops, and the kernel routing table has both subnets as directly connected entries. RIP is running correctly, advertising and receiving routes on all three interfaces. No iptables rules exist on `router0`, `cs_hod`, or `cs_lab1`. Both `switch0` and `switch1` have their bridge interfaces UP and their FDB tables are correctly populated with all host MACs. All five CS hosts (cs_hod 192.168.2.2 through cs_lab4 192.168.2.6) are reachable from `it_hod` with 0% packet loss and a single router hop (TTL=63), and the reverse path (cs_hod → it_hod) is equally healthy. The default gateways on both `it_hod` (→192.168.1.1) and `cs_hod` (→192.168.2.1) are correctly configured. No policy routing, no traffic-shaping drops, no ARP failures, and no RIP misconfigurations were found anywhere on the path.

The ticket's premise — that IT cannot reach CS — does not correspond to any actual network fault. The reported symptom is a false alarm; corrective action is to inform the user that connectivity is verified end-to-end and to investigate whether the issue was transient (e.g., a momentary ARP resolution delay at first contact) or a client-side application problem unrelated to the network infrastructure.
